content.text:
I made these changes to fix the GitHub Actions rate-limit failures:

1. [fetch.ts](src/artificial-analysis/fetch.ts) — on a `429` from Artificial Analysis, it now falls back to the cached `data/artificial-analysis/language-models.json` (logging a warning) instead of throwing, provided cached data exists. A genuine first-run failure (no cache to fall back to) still throws as before.

2. [daily.yml](.github/workflows/daily.yml) — the AA data wasn't previously persisted to the `data` branch at all (unlike provider pricing), so there was nothing to fall back to. Added seeding of `data-branch/latest/artificial-analysis` into `data/` before the run, and committing it back to both `latest/` and `history/YYYY-MM-DD/` afterward — mirroring the existing pricing fallback pattern.

3. [site/index.html](site/index.html) — the meta bar now fetches the AA data file and shows `Artificial Analysis data: <date>`, with the same `stale` badge logic already used for pricing sources, so a rate-limited run's stale data is visible on the page.

4. Updated [README.md](README.md:39) to reflect that AA data is now persisted and that a 429 no longer fails the run.

Verified with `tsc --noEmit` — no type errors.
